survey-tech: Primary survey; broad coverage signal, not an unbiased census or a route oracle.
survey-roles: Primary survey; role categories inform domain coverage; no market-share claim.
octoverse: Primary repository-activity report; contributor activity is not job/task frequency.
small-cl: Traditional engineering guidance, not a quantitative rule for section size.
pact: Actual consumer code versus a test-only client; no mandatory Pact adoption.
semver: Applies if the project adopts this versioning contract; not authority to add compatibility.
js: Language/host asynchronous composition and cancellation distinction.
ts: Static refinement; inspect runtime validation separately.
python: Current standard-library snapshot; actual interpreter version governs.
java: Language exception/resource handling; not a Spring contract.
csharp: Task composition and observation; actual target framework governs.
c: Examples of runtime UB detection; not complete proof or a required new sanitizer gate.
cpp: Ownership/RAII/interface guidance, not mandatory repository modernization.
go: Go cancellation/deadline propagation; does not prescribe a server architecture.
rust: Language resource ownership; no inference about Tokio.
cargo: Supported build configurations, not a Cartesian test mandate.
swift: Official source used because rendered docs are a JavaScript shell.
kotlin: Coroutine structure; actual kotlinx.coroutines dependency/configuration governs.
ruby: Reference API; deployed Ruby version governs.
dart: Event loop/isolate distinction; not a Flutter requirement.
sql: One database example only; never generalize its defaults to all SQL engines.
shell: Official indexed manual text; direct page fetch timed out. POSIX versus Bash is explicitly distinguished.
pwsh: Object pipelines and native-command boundaries; host/version matter.
lua: Specific reference; LuaJIT/Luau/host variants must be separately confirmed.
html: Browser form semantics; CSS/layout checks remain concrete browser evidence.
svelte: Form/action result encoding, not interchangeable with arbitrary JSON.
react: Derived state and avoiding redundant effects.
vue: Request isolation and hydration; Nuxt-specific APIs require installed-version evidence.
angular: Component initialization/update/destruction; not a change-detection migration mandate.
django-migration: Historical model state; inherited verified v4.5 source.
fastapi: Sync/async framework boundary; inspect actual dependency and client behavior.
spring: Proxy interception/self-invocation; configured rollback rules still need inspection.
spring-rollback: Inherited v4.5 source; configuration/version qualify defaults.
aspnet: Actual service lifetime and scope boundary.
rails: Callback/transaction placement; not proof of external-effect atomicity.
laravel: Job execution/retry/commit ordering in a versioned framework.
flutter: State/data responsibilities; recommendations are not obligatory migrations.
swiftui: Official indexed text supports source-of-truth/state/binding claims; dynamic page fetch was limited.
apple-distribution: Inherited v4.5 source; packaging/entitlements only when changed.
apple-scenes: Official indexed text describes UI instances/lifecycle; no beta API adoption.
android: Process/component lifecycle and state ownership; no mandatory app rewrite.
node: Completion/backpressure/resource ownership; not a language definition.
tokio-process: kill_on_drop is configurable; child lifecycle not proved by handle drop.
kubernetes: Deployment lifecycle example only; Kubernetes is not assumed.
airflow: Partitioned/retriable tasks as one implementation example.
ml: Pipeline/metric and training-serving concerns; not a requirement for a new ML platform.
pytorch: Official source fallback for redirected HTML; toolchain/device limits apply.
zephyr: ISR context restrictions as one RTOS example, not all devices.
godot: Different update clocks as one engine example.
openai-skills: Current official progressive-disclosure guidance; not evidence of this Skill performance.
claude-skills: Current official variation/reference guidance; not a new workflow requirement.
